system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded creation of it_helper, attributed to omar.haddad, at 13:46:31 UTC.
About two seconds after creation, it_helper was added to the domain Administrators group, with the same omar.haddad subject logon ID shown on the account-creation event.
The account name and administrator membership conflict with the stated help-desk practice of using tmp.<name> accounts in Temp-Staff only, and there is no other IT administrator besides omar.haddad.

At 13:42:58 UTC, the domain controller recorded a Kerberos service-ticket event for target user omar.haddad and service WS-BCARTER-01$, with source address 192.0.2.45; this address is outside the listed internal host ranges, and the inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-OHADDAD-01 with no VPN.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection on WS-BCARTER-01 was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, so workstation process and security-event evidence for that interval is missing.
Network and proxy telemetry was available, but it does not establish which process or person performed the account-management actions.
claims_not_established: The available evidence does not establish whether omar.haddad personally performed or authorized these changes, or whether the account was used or compromised by someone else.
The ticket event does not by itself establish who controlled source address 192.0.2.45 or prove that it caused the account changes.
The evidence does not show subsequent use of it_helper or the full scope of activity associated with it.
additional_evidence_needed: Validate whether creation of it_helper and its addition to Administrators had an approved change or business justification.
Collect endpoint and authentication evidence from WS-OHADDAD-01 and WS-BCARTER-01, including any recoverable logs for the 13:30–14:10 UTC collection outage.
Review domain-controller authentication and account-management audit details to determine the origin and execution context of the changes and whether the account was subsequently used.
Investigate the source and routing context for 192.0.2.45 and check for other authentication or administrative activity involving omar.haddad.
